title: The exchange identity: theta integrals of complementary rank agree up to a constant, and cruder forms complete a family to a basis in the lower bound
summary: Unit 147 (New/Exchange) proves the exchange theorem: for hermitian spaces V, V′ of complementary rank inside W, the theta integrals over U(V) and U(V′) of matched ramified data agree up to a non-zero constant whose squared absolute value is a fixed number times residue counts and products of partial Hecke L-values (`exchange_theorem`); it uses it for one square of lifts and transposed lifts, for the grid of such squares, and for the cruder forms of `Data.crude_rows`, which complete a family of target forms to a basis with integral twisted lifts and bounded conjugates in the lower bound (Theorem C). Chunk a (this dossier) holds the analytic and local foundations: the Rallis inner product of the adjoint lift θ_j^* and the L-value of the lift of the constant from U(1) (CharacterLiftNorm); local partner data and matched pairs (BlockPartners, PartnersMatch, StableSpaces); the vanishing of theta coefficients at forms that are not negative definite (NonnegativeVanishing); the equivariant functional of the difference of the two theta integrals and its vanishing on standard data (ExchangeDifference, StandardCoefficients); and the exchange identity at the top of the tower, from equal-rank constancy, matched real data and determinant vectors (LowRankIdentity, RealPair, DeterminantVectors).

members.name: AuxPair.adjoint_theta_eq_formLift
members.text: Let E be a field (`Field E`) which is a CM number field with a CM type (`CMType E`) and carries Weil data (`WeilData E`); let r, n be finite index types (`Fintype r`, `Fintype n`), r nonempty (`Nonempty r`), and O : AuxPair E r n an auxiliary pair, with W = W(O) its space of rank |r| and V = I_n the definite space. Let l be a parameter on W that fits O (h : FitsParams(O, l)), let y be a form on W of the type that the statement infers, and let z be an algebraic form on V of the level, character and weight of O (an element of FormV(O)) such that (a) for every Ξ in FormV(O) the inner product ⟨z, Ξ⟩ equals the Petersson product petersson(W, y, θ(O)(Ξ)), θ(O) the class-sum lift from V to W (`AuxPair.θ`). Then the function underlying z equals toAlgForm(I_n, isHCParam_paramV(O), formLift(pairThetaKernel(O), typeKernel(l, ·), ·, fockDatum(O, highestVector(κ(O), paramV(O))))(y)): the algebraic form, for the parameter paramV(O), of the theta lift of y to I_n by the datum v_{P_ξ} ⊗ Υ at the highest vector ξ of the weight of O.

members.text: Let E be a field which is a CM number field with a CM type and carries Weil data; let r, n be finite index types and O : AuxPair E r n an auxiliary pair with space W = W(O). Let v be a real datum (a vector of the Fock model at the infinite places) and y a function on U(W)(𝔸) which is rapidly decreasing and automorphic on W (hy : y ∈ rapidFunctions(W)) and fixed by the principal level at the chosen places M (h : HasLevel(y, levelOf(chosenPlace(O), ⊥)), i.e. by the elements of K₀ that reduce to 1 at every place of M). members.name: AuxPair.levelIndicator_support_and_normSq
members.text: Let E be a field which is a CM number field with a CM type, let r, n be finite index types and O : AuxPair E r n an auxiliary pair; let R = O_E/𝔪 be the residue ring of the modulus 𝔪 = levelModulus(O, 1), the product of the places of M and Q, and let F = #TwistGL(O, r)·levelIndicator(O), a function on n × r matrices over R (γ = #TwistGL(O, r) = ∏_{w∈Q} #GL_r(k_w)). Then (1) for every matrix y with F(y) ≠ 0 the rows of y indexed by incl(O) form the identity: inclMatrix(R, incl(O))ᵀ·y = 1; and (2) ∑_y |F(y)|² (the product star F ⬝ F) equals γ²·(∏_{i} q(twistPlace(O, i)))^{rankDiff(O)·|r|}, where q(w) is the norm of the place w and rankDiff(O) = |n| − |r|. (No Weil data is assumed.)

members.name: Data.rallisTerm
members.text: For parameters P, admissible data D for P, a tame character ϑ of D, signs s on the row index set and a hermitian space V = Space(E(D), RowIndex(D), s), a natural number j, two forms y′, y in principalForms(D, V) (forms of parameter ς fixed by the principal level at the chosen places above g) and a coset γ of the finite adelic group of rank n′ = |Y 1| = r + t modulo the elements integral off the places of 𝔪 = 𝔪(D, ϑ, 1) and their conjugates, rallisTerm(D, ϑ, j, V, y′, y, γ) is cosetTerm(|Y(D, 1)|, b(auxPair(D, ϑ, j)), (conjugate closure of the places of 𝔪(D, ϑ, 1))ᶜ, y′, y, γ) divided by #((Y(D, 1) × RowIndex(D)) → O_E/𝔪(D, ϑ, 1)). Here cosetTerm is ρ(g)⟨y′, R(g)y⟩ for the representative g of γ, ρ = vacuumCoeff of rank n′ for the character b = μ_j⁰ϑυ^{⌊n′/2⌋} of the j-th auxiliary pair and R the right translation; the divisor is #(O_E/𝔪)^{n′r}.

members.name: LValueData.inner_trivialLift_self_eq_L
members.text: Let E be a field which is a CM number field with a CM type and carries Weil data, n a finite index type, X : LValueData E n L-value data and k a natural number with 2k = |n| (hM) and k > 1 (hk), so |n| ≥ 4 is even. members.text: Let E be a field which is a CM number field with a CM type, with Weil data H (`WeilData E`; ȷ = H.j, υ = H.upsilonU1 its splitting character). Let a, b, m, n be finite index types; X : Space(E, m, r), Y : Space(E, n, s), Z : Space(E, a, t) hermitian spaces with signs r, s, t, and D a splitting of X over Z along b (`Space.Splitting X Z b`: X = (lE^b ⊕ kE^b) ⊥ iZ with isotropic frames l, k, l*Jk = 1, so rk X = rk Z + 2|b|). Let ν be a character of U(1)(𝔸) with weights μ and tame part ψ (`AutChar.HasWeight ν μ ψ`), δ a character, f a datum of the pair (X, Y), g a point of U(X)(𝔸) and T an n′ = b × b matrix over E. Assume: i is an index of Y with s(i) = 1 (Y has a positive sign); (hγ) μ(τ) < negCount(−t) for every infinite place τ (the weights of ν are below the number of positive signs of Z); (ht) |b| + negCount(t) = negCount(s) (Y has |b| more negative signs than Z); (d) δ = ν·υ^{|b|}; (h₀) T is invertible; (hR) T, read as an adelic matrix, is not represented by the form −1, i.e. at some infinite place τ there is no c with −c*c = T_τ (T_τ is not negative semidefinite); (hi) the theta terms of D for (Y, δ, δ, f, g) are integrable (`Space.Splitting.HasIntegrableTerms D Y δ δ f g`). Then the Fourier coefficient of the theta integral thetaIntegral(X, Y, δ, δ, f) at ȷT along the centre of the unipotent radical of D vanishes at g: centreCoeff(D, ȷ•T, thetaIntegral(X, Y, δ, δ, f), g) = 0.

There are a linear functional ℓ on the complex functions on GL_b(F) and a choice of representatives r_q ∈ GL_b(F) of the cosets q ∈ GL_b(F)/GL_b(O) such that: (1) for every finite set t of cosets and every function f with f(r_q) = 0 for all q ∉ t, ℓ(f) = ∑_{q∈t} f(r_q); and (2) for every n × b matrix y over F having a left inverse, there is exactly one coset q with y·r_q primitive (`IsPrimitiveMatrix O`: entries in O and a left inverse with entries in O), and exactly one coset q with y·r_q⁻¹ primitive.

members.name: IntegralFrame.partner_mem_of_unimodular_vanishing
members.text: Let F be a semilocal field (instance V) with compact open subring O and unit ϖ, a, b, m, n finite index types, χ a tame multiplicative character of F (instance hχ), e : b ⊔ a ≃ n, U a set of n × b matrices, P a GL_n(F)-stable space (hP) of Schwartz–Bruhat functions supported in U (hS), Φ, Ψ partners for χ over O with respect to e (Q) with Ψ locally constant (hΨ), A : IntegralFrame F n m b an integral frame (blocks K, I, L; K′, I′, L′), ψ an additive character of F with conductor O (hψ: ψ is continuous and ψ(tO) = 1 exactly when t ∈ O) and M a space of complex functions on n × b matrices. For z ∈ M_b(F) put S_z(y) = stdColDatum(χ, K′)(y + L·z·(K′·y)), so S₀ = stdColDatum(χ, K′). Suppose (1) every S_z lies in M, and (2) every Ψ′ ∈ M with the following property lies in P: Λ(Ψ′) = 0 for every b × b matrix T and every linear functional Λ such that Λ(S_z) = ψ(tr(T·z))·Λ(S₀) for all z and Λ(S₀) = 0 whenever T is primitive (unimodular). Then Ψ ∈ P.

members.statement_lean_full:
lemma IntegralFrame.partner_mem_of_unimodular_vanishing {ψ} {M : Submodule ℂ _} (hψ :
  HasIntegralConductor ψ) :
  let S (z : Matrix b b F) y := stdColDatum χ A.K' (y + A.L * z * (A.K' * y))
  (∀ z, S z ∈ M) →
    (∀ Ψ ∈ M, (∀ T (Λ : _ →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ), (∀ z, Λ (S z) = ψ (T * z).trace • Λ (stdColDatum χ
  A.K')) → (IsPrimitiveMatrix O T → Λ (stdColDatum χ A.K') = 0) → Λ Ψ = 0) → Ψ ∈ P) → Ψ ∈ P

members.name: exists_isEquivariantLift
members.text: Let E be a field which is a CM number field with a CM type and carries Weil data; n, a, b finite index types; W : Space(E, n, s) of even rank (hn: 2 divides |n|), V : Space(E, a, t), V′ : Space(E, b, t′) hermitian spaces; 𝔠 a split tame character of weight μ, with places S and local character χ_𝔠 at S; σ : b ⊔ a ≃ n; v, v′ rapid real data (hv, hv′: all weighted norms finite, `IsRapidDatum`); and c ∈ ℂ. There are a space M of complex functions on n × b matrices over the local product at S and a linear map 𝒟 from such functions to functions on U(W)(𝔸) such that (1) M, 𝒟 form an equivariant lift for 𝔠, W and the local character ρ = localChar(S, υ^{|b|}, |b|)⁻¹ (`IsEquivariantLift 𝔠 W ρ M 𝒟`: M consists of Schwartz–Bruhat functions supported on matrices with a left inverse; each 𝒟Ψ, Ψ ∈ M, is an automorphic function on U(W); for every finite adelic g supported at S, the translate Φ = Ψ((g_S)·) lies in M and 𝒟Φ(x g) = ρ(det g_S)·𝒟Ψ(x) for all x; and 𝒟Ψ is invariant under the elements of K_f trivial at S); and (2) for all partners Φ, Ψ for χ_𝔠 over O with respect to σ (`IsPartner O σ χ_𝔠 Φ Ψ`) with Ψ locally constant: Ψ ∈ M and 𝒟(Ψ) = thetaLarge(W, V, 𝔠, v, Φ) − c·thetaSmall(W, V′, 𝔠, v′, Ψ).

members.text: Let E be a field which is a CM number field with a CM type, with Weil data H (ȷ = H.j); n, a, b, m finite index types; s, t, r signs; 𝔠 a split tame character of weight μ (places S, local character χ_𝔠); ρ a character of the local product at S; X : Space(E, m, r), W₁ : Space(E, n, s), W : Space(E, a, t) hermitian spaces; M, 𝒟 an equivariant lift for 𝔠, X and ρ (h : IsEquivariantLift 𝔠 X ρ M 𝒟); D a splitting of X over W₁ along b and D₁ a splitting of W₁ over W along one line, both base-adapted (`IsBaseAdapted D`, `IsBaseAdapted D₁`); t′ signs and V′ : Space(E, b, t′). Let Ψ₀ = stdColDatum(χ_𝔠, L′) be the standard datum of the block L′ of the frame adaptedFrame(readsAt(𝔠), D). Assume (h₀): for all T, c, z, q, g, if either (i) there are an adelic b × b matrix Y and k ∈ GL_b(Ô_E) with scaleIdele(E)·x_{V′}·Y = q, (finite part of Y)·k unitary for the identity form, and J_{V′} = T, or (ii) T is invertible and, as an adelic matrix, not represented by t′ (RepresentedBy is the Gram equation at the infinite places: at some infinite place v there is no complex c with c*·diag(t′)·c = T_v), then the coefficient centreCoeff(D, ȷT, 𝒟(Ψ₀), radicalElt(D, c, z)·levi(D, (q, g))) vanishes; and assume (hΨ) Ψ₀ ∈ M. Then for every σ : b ⊔ b ⊔ n ≃ m and every matrix z with entries in O (i): 𝒟(stdColDatum(χ_𝔠, z)) = 0.

members.name: exists_contDiff_witt
members.text: Witt's theorem, smooth local form. Let b, m be finite index types, J an m × m complex matrix with J* = J (hJ), and x an m × b complex matrix whose Gram matrix x*Jx is invertible (d: det(x*Jx) ≠ 0). There is a map k from m × b matrices to the unitary group U(J) such that y ↦ k(y) (as a matrix) is smooth (C^∞ over ℝ) and, for every y near x, k(y)·x·c = y for some b × b matrix c: elements of U(J) depending smoothly on y carry the span of x to that of y near x.

members.text: Let E be a field which is a CM number field with a CM type and carries Weil data; n, n′, r, r′ finite index types; signs s, t on n, r and s′, t′ on n′, r′; natural numbers k and m(w); W : Space(E, n, s), W′ : Space(E, n′, s′), V : Space(E, r, t), V′ : Space(E, r′, t′); A a base-adapted splitting of W′ over W along one line and X a base-adapted splitting of V′ over V along one line (so W′, V′ are W, V plus a hyperbolic plane). Let β be a parameter and z a real number with z ≥ 1 (hz), and suppose rk W′ = 2(k + negCount(s′)) (hn). Then the cone integral at z with weights k + m, v′ ↦ ∫∫ coneIntegrand(A, X, k + m, β, z, v′, p) d(Haar × Haar)(p), is surjective from detVectors(k, m) (for (s′, t′)) onto detVectors(k, m) (for (s, t)) in the sense of Set.SurjOn: every determinant vector v of the smaller pair is the cone integral of some determinant vector v′ of the larger pair (the direction used when planes are removed). It is not asserted that the cone integral maps every determinant vector v′ into the determinant vectors of the smaller pair (no MapsTo).

members.text: Let E be a field which is a CM number field with a CM type, n a finite index type, s signs, W : Space(E, n, s) and S : Space(E, n, −s) a space with the opposite signs, and suppose (Γ) that the identification G.neg of the adelic unitary groups of signs s and −s carries the rational points of W onto those of S: G.neg(g) ∈ Γ(S) if and only if g ∈ Γ(W) (by default proved by simplification). members.text: Exchange theorem. Let E be a field which is a CM number field with a CM type and carries Weil data; n, a, b finite index types with signs s, t, t′; W : Space(E, n, s), V : Space(E, a, t), V′ : Space(E, b, t′); σ : b ⊔ a ≃ n (so rk W = rk V + rk V′); suppose negCount(s) = negCount(t) + negCount(t′) (hs), |a| = |b| + 2e for a natural number e (he), 2·negCount(s) + 2 ≤ |n| (hn); let μ be weights with |n| ≤ 2μ(v) + 2·negCount(s) at every infinite place v (hμ), and v a rapid real datum (hv). There are a real C and a rapid real datum x such that for every modulus 𝔪, character ν of U(1)(𝔸), and multiplicative character χ of O_E/𝔪 with IsTameFor(𝔪, ν, μ, χ) (𝔪 ≠ (1); ν of weight μ with tame part non-trivial exactly at the places of 𝔪; χ the product of its local tame parts), writing γ = rankTwist(ν⁻¹, n) = ν⁻¹υ^{⌊|n|/2⌋}: there is c ≠ 0 with |c|² = C·lValueProd(places(𝔪), ν, e) = C·(∏_{w∈S} Nw)^{e²}·∏_{j=1}^{e} |L^{S∪S̄}(j, BC ν)|², S = places(𝔪), where L^{S∪S̄}(·, BC ν) = ν.L(S, ·) is the Hecke L-function of the base change x ↦ ν(x/x̄) without the Euler factors at S and at the conjugate places (both products are 1 when e = 0), such that for all partners Φ, Ψ for χ over O_E/𝔪 with respect to σ (`IsPartner ⊤ σ χ Φ Ψ`) and every point g: thetaIntegral(W, V, γ, 1, modDatum(W, V, 𝔪, Φ, x))(g) = c·∫_{[U(V′)]} pairTheta(V′, W, γ, γ, modDatum(V′, W, 𝔪, Ψ, v), (h, g)) dh. C and x are chosen once, before the triple (𝔪, ν, χ); c depends on the triple only, and serves all partners and all g; only |c|² is specified. Here |n| = 2|b| + 2e.

members.name: LValueData
members.text: For a field E which is a CM number field with a CM type and a finite index type n: an element of LValueData(E, n) consists of level places of E (chosen places M and twist places Q), jet degrees dg (a natural number at each infinite place), a character μ of U(1)(𝔸) of weight τ ↦ −(dg(τ) + ⌊|n|/2⌋) with tame part ψ, the condition |n| > 1, and the unramifiedness ψ_w = 1 at every finite place w off the places. (The census's lines 91–98 of this structure end with line 98, `unseal Finset.univ in`, which is the prefix of the next declaration, LValueData.auxPair, not part of LValueData.)

members.text: For an index type I, a type V and a family F(i, n) of complex inner product spaces, V an inner product space, m ∈ ℕ, weights w(t, n) ∈ ℕ, a grading M (M(n, c) for families c : I → ℂ), linear arrows a(t, i, n) : F(i, n) → F(i, n + 1) and d(t, i, n) : F(i, n + 1) → F(i + 1, n), linear isometries j(i) : V → F(i, 0) and a proposition G: IsTriangle(m, w, M, a, d, j, G) holds when (1) M(0, 1); (2) M(n, c) and M(n′, c′) with n + n′ ≤ N give M(N, c·c′); (3) the square law: for i + (n + 1) < m there is β with w(t, n)·⟨z, a(t, ·, n)(d(t, i, n)y)⟩ = conj(β(t))⁻¹·w(t, n + 2)·⟨z, d(t, i, ·)(a(t, i, ·)y)⟩ for all t, y, z, and, under G, M(1, β) and there is κ with M(0, κ) and an adjoint law (for every t and z some x has ⟨a y, z⟩ = ⟨y, x⟩ for all y, and ⟨d x, y⟩ = κ(t)·⟨d z, a y⟩); (4) the first arrows: for i < m, a(t, i, 0)∘j(i) is adjoint to d(t, i, 0) on the images of j, and d(t, i, 0)(a(t, i, 0)(j(i)y)) = j(i + 1)(v) for some v with v = 0 only if y = 0.

members.name: one_square
members.text: One square: lift then descent is proportional to descent then lift. Let E be a field which is a CM number field with a CM type and carries Weil data; n, n′, n₁, n₂ finite index types with signs s, s′, s₁, s₂; A′ : Space(E, n, s), A : Space(E, n′, s′), U₁ : Space(E, n₁, s₁), U₂ : Space(E, n₂, s₂). Let I be an index set with families of characters a(i, ·), b(i, ·), ν(i), moduli 𝔪(i) and local characters χ(i), and suppose four edge families (`IsEdgeFamily`): h₂ for b from k₂ to k in direction d with datum Φ₂, h₁ for a from k₁ to k in direction ¬d with Φ₁, h₃ for a from k′ to k₂ in direction ¬d with Φ₂′, h₄ for b from k′ to k₁ in direction d with Φ₁′. Let σ be an identification of index sets, and assume negCount(s₁ ⊕ s₂) = negCount(s′) + negCount(s) (hs), |n′| = |n| + 2e (he), 2·negCount(s₁ ⊕ s₂) + 2 ≤ |n₁ ⊔ n₂| (hn), weights μ with |n₁ ⊔ n₂| ≤ 2μ(v) + 2·negCount(s₁ ⊕ s₂) at every infinite place (hμ), each ν(i) tame for 𝔪(i) with weights μ and character χ(i) (ht), and a(i, p)·b(i, q) = rankTwist(ν(i)⁻¹, n₁ ⊔ n₂) whenever |p| + |q| = |n₁| + |n₂| (hE). For a matrix x write u(i, x) = modDescent(·, A, b(i), Φ₂, δ_{x₂}) ∘ modLift(U₁, A, a(i), Φ₁, δ_{x₁}) (lift from U₁ to A, then descent to U₂, with point data at the column blocks x₁, x₂ of x), and for y write v(i, y) = modLift(A′, U₂, a(i), Φ₂′, δ_{y₂}) ∘ modDescent(·, ·, b(i), Φ₁′, δ_{y₁}) (descent from U₁ to A′, then lift to U₂, with point data at the row blocks of y). There are C and κ such that every i has c ≠ 0 with |c|² = C·lValueProd(places(𝔪(i)), ν(i), e) and, for every form f on U₁ and every linear functional l, SquareLaw(χ(i), σ, κ/c, x ↦ l(u(i, x)(f)), y ↦ l(v(i, y)(f))). (κ is not shown to be non-zero.)

members.name: Data.IsTidy.exists_square_move
members.text: Crossing a square. Let P, D, an m-fold twist ϑ, a grid z, indices a, b, n, a finite set w of ordered pairs of nodes and Λ ∈ GridDatum(ϑ); nodes p, v, Q, U, R, r; a finite type T, a type J; bijections τ : GridIndex(z, a, b) ≃ NodeIndex(U), σ : NodeIndex(p) ⊔ T ≃ NodeIndex(Q), ρ : NodeIndex(r) ⊔ T ≃ NodeIndex(R); an additive character ψ of the residue ring; a multiplicative character χ, a bijection ε and a constant C; and families L(i), M(i), i ∈ J, with SquareLaw(χ, ε, C, L(i), M(i)) for all i (q). Assume (hQ) every admissible family g has g(R) = blockInlGL(ρ, g(r)) and, for every k, the family u = g updated at p by k and at Q by blockInlGL(σ, k) is admissible with u(p) = k; (h) U ≠ v, (Q, U) is a μ-edge and (U, R) is not, or (p, v) is and (v, r) is not, the nodes U, R, v, r have index pairs at most (m, m) and are different from p and Q, and every edge of w has source outside {p, Q} and target outside {p, Q, R, r}; (H) Λ is tidy of order n on w ∪ {(p, v), (Q, U)}; and (X) χ = (edgeChar(ϑ, (p, v))·edgeChar(ϑ, (Q, U)))⁻¹, edgeChar(ϑ, (U, R)) = edgeChar(ϑ, (p, v)) and edgeChar(ϑ, (v, r)) = edgeChar(ϑ, (Q, U)). Then there is Φ, tidy of order n + 2 on w ∪ {(U, R), (v, r)}, such that for every f(S, k) ∈ J depending only on the values of S on w: Λ(S ↦ ∑_k ψ(tr(k·x₂))·M(f(S, k))((S(p, v); x₁))) = C·Φ(S ↦ L(f(S, x′₂))((S(v, r) | x′₁))), where x = S(Q, U) reindexed by τ, σ with column blocks x₁, x₂ and x′ = S(U, R) reindexed by ρ, τ with row blocks x′₁, x′₂.

literature.verdict: Constancy follows from strong approximation for the special unitary group together with the stated torus hypothesis.
literature.comparison: Kneser's Satz 2 gives density away from a set with a noncompact factor for the simply connected almost-simple classical group SU(W). The specified hyperbolic line makes SU(W) isotropic at every place, and S contains a finite place. For any fixed g, the continuous function h ↦ D(hg) on SU(W)(A) is invariant under rational elements on the left and under the full special unitary factor over a place in S on the right, since conjugation by g preserves that local subgroup. Density makes this function constant. This gives left invariance under SU(W)(A), hence under the unipotent radical. The additional hypothesis now removes the line-torus coordinate on the Levi. Every norm-one adelic determinant is t/t̄ by idelic Hilbert 90. The line Levi acts by t on one isotropic line and t̄⁻¹ on its dual, so each element agrees in determinant with such a Levi element. This proves D(g)=D(1). The given integral level away from S is compatible with the argument. Kneser applies to SU(W), and the torus premise supplies the passage to U(W).

imports.text: Fourier uniqueness on a compact quotient: let the χ_i form a dual family of characters of B modulo the lattice B₀ and let F be continuous and B₀-periodic. If the mean of χ_i·F over the quotient vanishes for every i such that χ_i(a) = c whenever c·F(x + a) = F(x) for all x, then F = 0. (The hypothesis is weaker than the vanishing of all Fourier coefficients ∫ χ_i·F: for the other i the coefficient vanishes by itself. `literature`: specializes.)

literature.verdict: Compact-quotient Fourier uniqueness with an explicit reduction to the compatible characters.
literature.comparison: For a continuous periodic F, Lean requires the vanishing of the mean of χ_i F only at those i for which every identity c F(x+a)=F(x) implies χ_i(a)=c. At every other i, translation invariance of the mean forces the coefficient to vanish, since it is multiplied by two different scalars. The character family contains constants, separates points of the compact quotient and is closed under multiplication and conjugation. Its span is dense by Stone–Weierstrass. Vanishing of the coefficients therefore forces the measure F times Haar measure to vanish and continuity gives F=0 pointwise. The classical uniqueness theorem applies after this reduction.

literature.comparison: For a Hermitian CM space the unitary group over the real subfield is smooth, connected and rational: the Cayley transform identifies dense opens of the skew-adjoint endomorphisms and the unitary group in characteristic zero. literature.verdict: Orthonormalization of a unimodular integral Hermitian matrix at all finite places.
literature.comparison: The ring here is the integral finite adèles of a CM field containing a primitive 5040th root. The pin produces an integral z with z−z* a unit. Thus conjugation cannot act trivially on the residue field at a nonsplit prime fixed by it, excluding ramification in the quadratic extension of the real subfield. At an unramified nonsplit place Wall's classification gives a unique unimodular lattice of each rank, hence a basis with identity Gram matrix. At a split pair the Hermitian pairing is an ordinary perfect pairing of free modules on the two factors, where one chooses dual bases. The local changes of basis and their inverses assemble in the product of the local integer rings. Equality of field discriminant classes alone would not imply integral equivalence at ramified dyadic places.

literature.comparison: Mínguez's Theorem 1 for GLₙ × GLₘ over a nonarchimedean field, n≤m and D=F, gives the contragredient parameter plus the parameter of the trivial GLₘ₋ₙ representation for the irreducible theta correspondent. This accounts for the dual input and the extra string of roots at an eigencharacter. Lean assumes a split place w, two characters unramified there, the projection-to-vacuum condition on f, m=n+k, and a linear map equivariant on the indicated translates of f. Its image is spherical for both actions. On this vector it identifies the output polynomial at w with the input polynomial at the conjugate place, evaluated at q^k A/B times X, multiplied by ∏_{j<k}(1−q^j A X). Here A and B are the respective space-character uniformizer values times q^{n/2} and q^{m/2}. Arbitrary ambient representations and possible nonsimple Hecke modules make a scalar-eigenvalue comparison insufficient. The source proves the vector identity by local residue-matrix sums.

literature.verdict: The exact shape and rank range of the classical identity are verified. The test spaces and volume normalization differ.
literature.comparison: Li, Theorem 2.1, equation (26), expresses the inner product of two theta lifts as an integral of the product of a Weil matrix coefficient and an automorphic matrix coefficient. In Li's quadratic-extension case, ε = 1/2, hence his n > 2n′ + 4ε − 2 is precisely target rank > twice source rank. His two source vectors belong to one cuspidal representation and both Weil vectors are Schwartz–Bruhat functions. Lean allows two arbitrary rapidly decreasing automorphic functions, a free second datum f′ and a clean first datum. Clean means constant signature sign, or finite test data on conjugately disjoint places supported on matrices left-invertible at a specified place. The Lean conclusion includes integrability and the target quotient volume for its Haar measures. Comparing Li's choices of measure and extending his stated hypotheses to these spaces remain necessary. Liu's Proposition 2.3 unfolds a cuspidal Eisenstein zeta integral for Re(s)>n and decomposable data. Eischen–Harris–Li–Skinner 4.1.4 is a section on cuspidal zeta integrals.

imports.text: For a character ν of U(1)(𝔸) of non-zero weight e (with some tame part) and a finite set S of places, the partial L-value ν.L(S, s) — the Hecke L-function of the base change x ↦ ν(x/x̄) to the ideles of E, without the Euler factors at S ∪ S̄ — is non-zero for every real s ≥ 1 (`literature`: specializes Hecke non-vanishing on Re s ≥ 1).

literature.verdict: Real-axis specialization of Hecke nonvanishing for a nonzero angular weight vector, with a finite Euler-factor adjustment.
literature.comparison: For a CM field E with a CM type, ν an automorphic character of the norm-one torus with weight vector e and tame part ψ, e≠0 means at least one component is nonzero. For a finite set S of finite primes and real s≥1 the project asserts ν.L S s≠0. Its unitary Hecke character is χ(x)=ν(x/x̄); the angular type of χ is 2e, so χ² is nontrivial. The primitive finite L-function is nonzero on Re(s)=1 by Ramakrishnan and Valenza, Theorem 7-28, and for Re(s)>1 by the absolutely convergent Euler product. The project defines a function of real s by extension from s>1. It suppresses S∪S̄ and takes χ at a chosen uniformizer at every other prime, even a ramified prime. The latter differs from the conventional primitive ramified factor 1. There are finitely many such primes, and each added or removed factor is invertible near each real s≥1 since |χ(π)|=1 and Nπ>1. This also identifies the right-limit value at 1. The stated boundary and the nonquadratic case are narrower than the published nonvanishing theorem. Tate's cited Main Theorem 4.4.1 gives meromorphic continuation and the functional equation; the boundary nonvanishing requires a further argument.
sources: D. Ramakrishnan and R. J. Valenza, Fourier Analysis on Number Fields (1999), §7.7, Theorem 7-28, p. 289 and (7.16), proof pp. 289–292, including the nonquadratic case. This gives the precise nonvanishing theorem and reduction to the finite L-function. <https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~julien.marche/Ref_GL_GT/Fourier_Analysis_on_Number_Fields.pdf>

J. Tate, Fourier analysis in number fields and Hecke's zeta-functions, Cassels–Fröhlich, ch. XV, §4.4, Main Theorem 4.4.1, p. 339, for the global zeta-integral continuation and exceptional poles. <https://www.scribd.com/document/36184190/Cassels-Froehlich-Eds-Algebraic-Number-Theory-378s>

literature.comparison: The output fixes the given rational frame k exactly. It supplies a dual isotropic frame l with l*Jk=1, an orthogonal inclusion of the complement, the rank equality, and a Space on the complement. Space includes an adelic frame with the specified signs at infinity and identity Gram matrix at finite places. literature.comparison: Fix any translate x and an open subgroup K contained in the standard compact K₀ at the finite places. For the continuous cusp kernel e and the rational subgroup Γ, a bounded continuous K-fixed form k reproduced by e satisfies conjugate(k(g))=Σγ e((xγg)∞)1_K((xγg)f) at every g. The assertion allows k=0. Godement’s Théorème 5 works on the Siegel domain for holomorphic H¹ sections, and 5 bis assumes a K-finiteness condition and the bound on lowest weight. Muić’s Theorems 6-4 and 7-6 concern integrable discrete series with a specified K-finite vector and smooth cuspidal vectors. Neither theorem identifies every continuous kernel here. Muić’s Lemma 6-3 provides an argument that adapts directly. Write e=α*e with α continuous and compactly supported. A translate of the compact support of α⊗1_K meets a Γ-coset in uniformly boundedly many points, by finiteness of Γ intersected with the product of the support and its inverse. Periodize the translate of conjugate(α)⊗1_K, then convolve at infinity with e. The uniform multiplicity bound and ‖e‖₁ justify interchange, give a bounded continuous sum, and e*e=e gives reproduction. The Hermitian involution yields the conjugation in the formula. The cited quantifiers for smooth or holomorphic input still differ from the pinned theorem.

literature.verdict: Godement’s finite-dimensionality lemma in Borel §8.3 applies after the project’s uniform height bound and compactness criterion. Harish-Chandra’s fixed-type theorem in §8.4 has different hypotheses.
literature.comparison: For any open subgroup K of the finite adelic unitary group, the bounded continuous rationally invariant forms fixed by K and reproduced by e form a finite-dimensional complex space. The full IsCuspKernel hypotheses are those at RealConvolution.lean:74–77, and K may contain a smaller compact open subgroup K′. Borel §8.4 fixes a finite-codimensional ideal of the center of the enveloping algebra and a standard idempotent for a maximal compact group. The Lean assumptions specify neither. There is an independent route from §8.3. The project proves finite quotient volume and, for fixed K′ and e, |F(g)|·height(g)≤R‖F‖∞. Mahler compactness puts a representative of every coset with height at most 2R in one compact set C, and outside this set modulo rational translates |F|≤‖F‖∞/2. On C, F=R(α)F for the compactly supported continuous α satisfying α*e=e. Averaging also over K′, Cauchy–Schwarz bounds |F| by a constant times its quotient L² norm, since the support swept out by C, supp α and K′ is compact and its rational translates have uniformly finite overlap.
